text: `curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/` gives connection refused, but the process is definitely running (`pgrep nginx` shows it). This isn't a crashed service -- it's listening somewhere, just not where clients look. List every address:port nginx actually holds: `sudo ss -tlnp`.

`ss -tlnp` shows nginx bound to `127.0.0.2:8080`, not `127.0.0.1:8080`. `127.0.0.2` is a valid loopback address (all of `127.0.0.0/8` is loopback), but nothing outside the box -- or even `curl localhost` on this box -- targets it by default. Find the config: `grep -rn listen /etc/nginx/`.

`/etc/nginx/conf.d/app.conf` has `listen 127.0.0.2:8080;`. Change it to `listen 127.0.0.1:8080;` (or `listen 0.0.0.0:8080;` if you want it reachable on every local address), then validate and reload without dropping connections: `sudo nginx -t && sudo nginx -s reload`.
Re-test: `curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/`. Confirm with `sudo ss -tlnp` that nginx now shows up on `127.0.0.1:8080` (or `0.0.0.0:8080`).
